transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-24
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes approx
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Leah (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (NexaLead), Tom (Nexa Platform), Marta (Nexa Sec), Alex (Prod)

Summary:
Quick weekly pilot check-in focused on choosing candidate model variants to pin for the pilot, defining cutover criteria (latency, quality regression tolerances), and planning an engineered fallback path. Agreed to run an engineered benchmark and exchange sanitized traces.

Topics:
- Model variant comparison (open model vs quantized variant)
- Version pinning granularity (route-level vs account-level)
- Soft-fallback / emergency cutover playbook
- Security concerns for Private deployment and KMS integration
- Benchmark plan and next steps

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir: Alright everyone, thanks for carving out time. We'll do quick status, then Leah will walk through the benchmark plan and the model matrix we prepared. Priya how are things on your side?
[00:18] Priya: Good, thanks. We got the small sample set uploaded, it's masked but we still need to clean up a couple of fields, I'll finish that today. Wanted to focus on which variants we should plan to "lock" for the first cutover.
[00:32] Leah: Cool. We've got three candidates: base-7b-fp16 (open), base-7b-4bit (quantized), and a tuned 6.9b safety-trimmed variant. The tradeoffs are classic: fp16 has best quality, 4bit wins cost and throughput but has slight diffs on edge cases.
[00:50] Tom: When you say slight diffs, can you give a rough metric? A/B or rouge-like?
[00:56] Leah: Good q. From our internal eval on your prompt set, BLEU-ish style metric — or rather exact match on critical fields — the 4bit had about 2.5% drift on slot-filling accuracy vs fp16. In free-form summarization it's noisier, maybe 3-6% on our heuristic.
[01:15] Diego: Also important: quantized variant shows 30-40% lower p99 latency under continuous batching in our infra, cost per token down ~45%. But as Priya's team flagged, we need to confirm hallucination profile doesn't spike on your clinical instructions.
[01:30] Priya: Right, clinical false positives are our biggest risk. If drift hits above 3%, procurement won't sign off. We need a clear rollback trigger.
[01:41] Samir: That makes sense. Proposal: pin the fp16 as the canonical route for high-sensitivity queries and route low-risk conversational traffic to the 4bit variant as default. We can define policies by route tags or by thresholding on request type.
[01:58] Alex: Implementation effort? We want minimal code changes.
[02:03] Leah: On Redwood, you can pin per-route in the catalog with a single config change. Two options: account-level pin (simpler) or route-level pin (more precise). Route-level needs adding a header or route key but no heavy infra changes.
[02:18] Tom: We'd prefer route-level if it's not a major lift; we already tag routes in the gateway.
[02:25] Leah: Perfect, then we'll prepare the route pins. We'll also enable soft-fallbacks — that's key.
[02:31] Marta: Quick security check: if we enable soft-fallbacks, how do logs and KMS behave when we fail to a hosted model?
[02:40] Diego: Good point. For Private deployment, logs stay in your VPC and keys are customer-managed HSM or KMS. For Hosted fallback, you can choose masked logging and disable payload persistence. We'll document retention differences.
[02:55] Marta: We need that in writing for SOC 2 audit, please.
[02:58] Samir: We'll attach the security annex. I'll follow up with the exact doc.
[03:03] Leah: Walkthrough of the benchmark plan: 1) run 2-hour steady-state simulation with your trace mix, 2) do 1-hour ramp with spikes to validate cold starts, 3) run a quality pass with 500 sampled outputs for manual review. We'll compare p50/p90/p99, token throughput, and the heuristic quality score.
[03:26] Priya: That sounds good. Can Redwood run both fp16 and 4bit back-to-back? We want apples to apples.
[03:31] Leah: Yes — we'll use identical request order, same batching policy; only the model variant changes. We'll capture KV cache behavior too, though for these short prompts it's minimal.
[03:42] Tom: On KV cache — last time we saw a mismatch in prefix caching between variants. Could that affect latency?
[03:47] Diego: If model vocab or tokenizer differences change prefix sizes, yes. We'll normalize tokenization and force the same tokenizer pipeline during benching. Noted as a risk.
[03:55] Alex: On rollback criteria — we need a mechanical definition so we can automate a failover. What's Redwood's standard SLO for triggering an emergency rollback?
[04:05] Leah: We typically set a triad: 1) Quality delta above threshold (e.g., >3% on critical metric), 2) Error rate spike (5x baseline), or 3) Latency p99 breach by >200ms for 10 consecutive minutes. Any single trigger can start an automated rollback to the pinned variant.
[04:25] Priya: The quality delta is the one we'll fight over. Can we get a real-time monitor and a daily sampled human-check?
[04:32] Diego: Yes, Redwood Optimize and Console can push heuristics and sample outputs to your review queue; we can wire an alert to your Slack channel.
[04:40] Samir: Also important — hotfix path: if the pinned model needs a patch (e.g., bad regression), we support 'hot swap' to a previous version with a short TTL while you validate. That's the escape hatch.
[04:52] Alex: Does that require schema changes in the app?
[04:55] Leah: No schema change. We use the version gateway to route by model tag; swap is a config flip.
[05:01] Marta: Auditing: every swap needs an entry in the audit log for compliance. Is that automatic?
[05:06] Diego: Yes audit logs capture change, user, timestamp, and the antecedent model version. For private customers, logs are pushed to your SIEM endpoint on request.
[05:15] Priya: On the topic of fallback economics — if we default to 4bit for low-risk, then sometimes fallback to hosted fp16 will incur cost delta; can we have a spend cap?
[05:27] Samir: We can enforce budget limits and alert on crossing thresholds. We also recommend warm standby capacity for Dedicated customers to avoid cross-tier network costs on emergency failovers.
[05:40] Tom: For the pilot we want to simulate the spend behavior so procurement can sign off.
[05:44] Leah: We'll include cost-per-1000-token projections for both steady state and failover scenarios in the benchmark output.
[05:52] Priya: Any concerns about hallucination rates specific to quantized variants on medical templates?
[05:57] Leah: Slightly higher hallucination on structured extraction—our heuristic shows more false insertions on inferred fields. We'll flag those and the manual review batch will focus on that.
[06:08] Alex: Ok let's talk timeline for pinning. We want to lock the first set of routes by next Tuesday and run canary for 48 hours.
[06:18] Samir: Sounds good. Proposed schedule: Benchmarks this week, review on Mon, pin Tues, 48-hr canary wed-thu, then full traffic Fri if no regressions.
[06:28] Priya: That's aggressive but okay if bench results are clean.
[06:31] Leah: On the Canary gating, we'll set the gate to fail if the canary shows >2% degradation on critical slot accuracy or p99 latency regresses >150ms. That's slightly tighter than the emergency threshold.
[06:45] Tom: For instrumentation — can we get per-route token breakdowns and cost per route?
[06:50] Diego: Yes Console provides per-route token costs and latency histograms. We'll share a dashboard link after the bench run.
[06:57] Samir: Quick note on private vs hosted fallback: if you do Private primary + Hosted fallback, you'll need explicit acceptance on data flow to Hosted during fallback. Marta, you'd want a legal statement?
[07:09] Marta: Absolutely. We need explicit conditions defined, and minimal logging when that flow is used. Also SSO and RBAC mapping must be preserved.
[07:17] Samir: We'll include legal language and RBAC mapping steps.
[07:20] Alex: Anything on model governance — who approves a pin? Is it our PM + Redwood AE?
[07:25] Leah: We'd recommend a small governance board: Product Owner (Alex), ML Lead (Priya), Security (Marta), and Redwood SE (Leah). That group signs off before cutting full traffic.
[07:36] Priya: Fine. Regarding AB tests during canary — can Redwood run shadow traffic routing for statistical comparison?
[07:44] Diego: Yes, we support shadowing and side-by-side full fidelity comparisons. We can also run significance tests on metrics and produce a short report.
[07:53] Priya: Great.
[07:55] Samir: Any blockers from your side for the benchmark?
[07:58] Tom: We need a 2-hour maintenance window for VPC peering and a contact. I'll confirm the window by Friday.
[08:05] Marta: Security doc please.
[08:07] Samir: Will send.
[08:09] Leah: We'll also include a short troubleshooting playbook: 1) detect regression, 2) auto fallback to pinned model, 3) notify governance, 4) run hotfix validations, 5) roll back or roll forward.
[08:23] Alex: For the hotfix validation, how long typically to verify a patch?
[08:27] Leah: Usually 2–4 hours for smoke tests, longer if human review required.
[08:31] Priya: One more question: tokenizer differences you mentioned — is there an easy way to enforce identical tokenization across model versions?
[08:38] Diego: We can enforce a tokenizer preprocessor in the request pipeline — same byte pair encoding/rope config. We'll include that in the bench.
[08:48] Samir: Okay let's summarize next steps.
[08:50] Samir: Redwood: Leah to run the benchmark (2 hours steady + spike + 500-sample quality check) and share raw CSV + dashboard by 2026-03-01.
[08:59] Samir: Redwood: Samir to send security annex and updated pricing comparison by 2026-02-26.
[09:06] Samir: Customer: Priya to provide sanitized traces and PII redaction rules by 2026-02-27.
[09:11] Samir: Customer: Tom to confirm VPC peering window by 2026-02-28.
[09:17] Alex: Cool. Anything else?
[09:19] Priya: Please include an explicit example of the rollback API call in the playbook so our on-call can trigger it with one command.
[09:27] Leah: We'll add a curl example in the playbook and a sample terraform snippet for route pin.
[09:34] Samir: Great, thanks everyone. We'll reconvene after the bench.
[09:38] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-attribution and a few words garbled around tokenizer/rope configs. Shared artifacts: 1) Benchmark template: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/nexahealth-2026-02 (private link), 2) Security annex draft (will be attached to follow up email).
